newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE REMAIN CONFIDENT DESPITE MANY INJURIES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE REMAIN CONFIDENT DESPITE MANY INJURIES.

text.p: France, who have lost five players, including captain Philippe St Andre, through injury in the past few days, still believe they can put together a team capable of challenging the Springboks.
Of the 26 players who gathered at a training camp in Narbonne on Tuesday, only 21 were still available on Friday for the first test against the South Africans in Bordeaux on November 30.

St Andre, winger Emile Ntamack, locks Olivier Merle and Olivier Roumat and prop Jean-Louis Jordana will all have to be left out. Prop Christian Califano joined the casualty list on Friday when he suffered a calf injury.

"It's true that we have been unlucky but I'm not too worried," said coach Jean-Claude Skrela, who will announce his team on Saturday in Brive after the Springboks' opening tour match against the French Barbarians.
"We have still got enough talented players left to build a strong team."
Abdelatif Benazzi and Fabien Pelous, who can both play either in the back row or lock, are the two favourites to replace St Andre as captain.
"We have two candidates to replace Philippe for the first test but just for that match because he will stay our captain at least until the end of the season," said French manager Jo Maso.

"All those on the pitch in Bordeaux will give all they have," said Maso. "I'm confident. We respect the Springboks and I can assure you that the team we pick to play them will not be a second choice one."
